_comment: Canals: type locks (Panama, the Great Lakes systems) or convoy (Suez). Every canal has path (its centerline, [lon, lat], laid exactly into the lanes that cross it by tools/build_map_data.gd), divide (a line along the land between the two sides that crosses path once: a lane crossing it an odd number of times goes through the canal), toll_share (of a leg's base pay, charged on entering; with a convoy, as it leaves; ships without the money wait) and xp_bonus (added to other bonuses on the delivery; a leg through several canals gets them all). directions names the two ways through, along path then back. LOCKS: locks lists each lock in path order with its chambers (points on path), rises_forward, and lanes: each_way (a lane each way, like Panama and Welland 4-6) or shared (one ship at a time either way, with parallel side-by-side chambers, like the Soo). A shared chamber is left at the level for the other way, so the next ship the same way waits step_seconds while it's turned around; with ships waiting both ways they alternate. Ships line up queue_spacing_nm apart for a busy chamber, and stay in an each_way chamber for the next when it's each_way too and within hold_chamber_nm. CONVOY: ships wait at anchor (anchorages: [first end, second end] as [lon, lat], named by anchorage_names) until a convoy leaves, every convoy_interval_s both ways at once (or join within convoy_grace_s after), then enter fastest first at speed_factor of their speed, convoy_spacing_nm apart; double lists the doubled stretches as [first, last] path indices, where ships can pass and where convoys meet: a ship won't enter a single-lane stretch with an oncoming ship in it, and keeps behind the ship ahead in one. lighten: {model id: share of cargo it must unload to pass} (its pay for the leg drops by that). labels: [[text, lon, lat]] shown zoomed in. OLDER NOTES (Panama): Canals with locks. path is the canal's centerline as [lon, lat] points from its first end to its second (Panama: Atlantic to Pacific); tools/build_map_data.gd carves it as water and lays it into every sea lane that crosses the canal, so ships follow it exactly. Every lock chamber must also be a point on path. Chambers are spaced about 1.5 nm apart, several times real size, so they show up at full zoom (like the ships, which are drawn much bigger than life). locks lists each set of chambers in path order; rises_forward says whether a ship sailing along path (Atlantic to Pacific) goes up in it (Gatun lifts ships to Gatun Lake, Pedro Miguel and Miraflores lower them to the Pacific). Each chamber has two lanes, one per direction, and holds one ship per lane for step_seconds while the water rises or falls. Ships wait in line queue_spacing_nm apart before a busy chamber, engines off (no fuel, no wear); a ship that finishes a chamber stays in it until the next one is free if that one is at most hold_chamber_nm further on. Nothing breaks down inside the canal. Entering the canal costs toll_share of the leg's base pay (before hub bonuses); a ship without the money waits at the entrance. Deliveries from a leg through the canal earn xp_bonus more XP for the company, the ship and the hub where they're unloaded (added to other bonuses). Recovery boats use the locks but pay no toll. directions names the two ways through (along path, then back), for the lock popup. divide is a line along the land between the two seas (crossing the canal once, at the Culebra Cut): the map tool treats any lane that crosses it as going through the canal, and cuts out lanes' detours across it and back.
